title: Conjecture 3.5
statement_text: There is an integer $\ell$ such that if $G$ is a directed-triangle-free digraph with $\alpha(G) = \alpha$, then $\gamma(G) \leq \alpha^{\ell}$.
context_text: All digraphs here are finite, loopless and simple in the sense that between any two vertices there is at most one arc (so no 2-cycles). The independence number $\alpha(G)$ of a digraph $G$ is the independence number of its underlying undirected graph. A vertex dominates itself and all its out-neighbours; a set $S$ of vertices is dominating if every vertex is in $S$ or is an out-neighbour of some vertex of $S$, and the domination number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set. A digraph is directed-triangle-free if it contains no directed (cyclically oriented) triangle. The dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}(G)$ is the minimum number of colours in a colouring of the vertices in which every colour class induces an acyclic digraph. The authors prove that every digraph on $n$ vertices has $\gamma(G)\le\alpha(G)\log n$ (and fractional domination number at most $2\alpha(G)$), but $\gamma$ cannot in general be bounded by a function of $\alpha$ alone (random tournaments have domination number of order $\log n$). For directed-triangle-free digraphs it can: the domination number is at most $\alpha(G)\cdot\alpha(G)!$, and at most $3$ when $\alpha(G)=2$. The same authors previously conjectured that the dichromatic number of a directed-triangle-free digraph is bounded by a polynomial in $\alpha(G)$; since every acyclic digraph has a kernel (an independent dominating set), $\gamma(G)\le\alpha(G)\cdot\vec{\chi}(G)$ for every digraph, so that conjecture would imply this one. A disjoint union of cyclically oriented pentagons shows that one cannot do better than $\gamma(G)\le\frac{3}{2}\alpha(G)$ in general.
notes: The hypothesis uses $\alpha(D) = \alpha$ in the PDF source, but the digraph is consistently called $G$ throughout the paper; this appears to be a typo for $\alpha(G) = \alpha$.
paper_title: Domination and fractional domination in digraphs
